item.title: SHERIFF’S LOG
item.description: The Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office (JCSO) responded to a total of 268 calls for service from Jan. 14-20. Deputies conducted 93 traffic stops, of which five resulted in criminal (misdemeanor/felony) charges. JAN. 14: More than $12,000 worth of copper telephone cable was stolen from telephone poles in Brinnon. The location was photographed. No suspects. item.title: POLICE LOG
item.description: The Port Townsend Police Department (PTPD) logged a total of 207 calls from Jan. 9-16. PTPD conducted 43 traffic stops, one of which resulted in infractions being issued, and took six reports of traffic collisions, none of which incurred injuries, but a majority of which entailed larger property damage. item.description: Law enforcement is still on the lookout for a suspect or suspects in the Jan. 11 theft of a white, two-door 1991 Ferrari from the Gardiner area. item.title: Chimney fire contained at Port Townsend’s American Legion Hall
item.description: A chimney fire at the American Legion Hall in Port Townsend was contained on the evening of Jan. 22, with no injuries or damage to the outside structure, according to East Jefferson Fire Rescue. item.title: BRIEFS
item.description: Bridge closure The SR 104 Hood Canal Bridge will be closed from 10 p.m. to 11:59 p.m. on Jan. 29 as crews conduct emergency storm training. Intermittent closures of up to 30 minutes are expected. The training was scheduled for the evening to minimize traffic disruptions. During the training, crews will practice securing the bridge during a severe weather event. […] The post BRIEFS first appeared on Port Townsend & Jefferson County Leader.

item.title: Quilcene School Board rescinds trans athlete resolution
item.description: Keeping their campaign promises, newly elected Quilcene School Board members Richard Fitzgerald and Naomi Stern led the charge in rescinding the board’s May 2025 resolution to prevent transgender athletes from competing in school sports with the gender they identify with. Fitzgerald made the motion an hour into the board meeting on Jan. 21. item.title: County secures nearly $3 million for homeownership
item.description: Three projects in Jefferson County will receive nearly $3 million in state funding to support affordable homeownership opportunities. item.description: A nearly $1 million state infrastructure grant will allow Habitat for Humanity of East Jefferson County to move forward this September with its long-awaited Mason Street affordable housing neighborhood, a project that is slated to bring 138 homes to Port Hadlock by the end of 2030.
